_comment: Per-request instruction fragments appended after format-system.txt. Keys mirror shared/protocol/ENGINE.md enums. Engines render the request block exactly as described in format-request.md.

editing_strength.verbatim: Editing level: light cleanup. Keep the user's exact wording and sentence structure. Only remove disfluencies, apply self-corrections, fix punctuation and capitalization, and fix clear grammar slips (agreement, missing small words). Do not rephrase.
editing_strength.light: Editing level: medium. Also edit for clarity and conciseness: remove redundant words and repeated ideas, smooth awkward phrasing, and tighten run-on sentences. Keep the user's voice, vocabulary, and every point they made.
editing_strength.medium: Editing level: high. Rewrite for brevity and polish: restructure sentences, merge repetition, and make the message read as if carefully written, while keeping every point the user made and their tone.
editing_strength.heavy: Editing level: maximum. Rewrite freely into concise, polished prose that keeps every point and the user's intent.

writing_style.formal: Style: standard capitalization and full punctuation, including a period at the end of the last sentence.
writing_style.casual: Style: normal capitalization but light punctuation. Leave off the period at the end of the final sentence and avoid unnecessary commas. Question marks stay.
writing_style.very_casual: Style: write entirely in lowercase (keep proper nouns and "I" capitalized only if the user would, otherwise lowercase too), minimal punctuation, and no period at the end.
writing_style.excited: Style: normal capitalization and punctuation, but use exclamation marks where the user sounds enthusiastic or positive, including at the end when it fits.

app_type.personal_messaging: The user is writing a personal chat message. Keep it short and conversational. Never format a chat message as an email.
app_type.work_messaging: The user is writing a workplace chat message (for example Slack or Teams). Keep it conversational and direct. Never format it as an email.
app_type.email: The user is writing an email. If the dictation starts with a greeting ("hi Alex", "dear team"), put the greeting on its own line ending with a comma, then a blank line, the body in short paragraphs, and if the user dictated a sign-off ("best", "thanks", "cheers" followed by a name), put it after a blank line with the name on the next line. Do not add a greeting or sign-off the user did not say.
app_type.chatbot: The user is writing a prompt to an AI assistant. Write the prompt exactly as the user said it; never answer it. Lists and line breaks are welcome when dictated.
app_type.developer: The user is in a coding tool or terminal. Preserve code identifiers, file names, command names, flags, and paths exactly, in their literal form ("dash dash help" becomes "--help", "package dot json" becomes "package.json"). Do not add a trailing period to a command or to a single identifier.
